Corollary
[Existence of the geometric limit flow] ↗ thm:asymptotic-gradient-shrinking-soliton ↗ def:kappa-noncollapsed

After passage to a subsequence, the flows $(M,g_k(t),(q_k,-1))$ converge smoothly on $-\infty <t<0$ to a complete flow $(M_\infty ,g_\infty (t),(q_\infty ,-1))$ with nonnegative curvature operator. It is $\kappa $-non-collapsed on all scales and satisfies $\partial _tR\geq 0$.
Proof

\sketch The preceding bounds control $l_{x_k}$ and hence $R_{g_k}$ on every fixed based ball and every interval bounded away from $t=0$. Nonnegative curvature controls $\Rm $, and non-collapsing plus Theorem flowlimit gives a limit. Diagonalization in the final time cutoff yields the full interval; curvature sign, non-collapsing, and the Harnack consequence pass to the limit.

□
